examples.en: The size doesn't fit, so I'm exchanging the clothes.

examples.ko: 어제 산 신발을 다른 색으로 교환했어요.
examples.en: I exchanged the shoes I bought yesterday for another color.

examples.ko: 이 상품은 일주일 안에 교환하실 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can exchange this item within a week.
I swapped phone numbers with my friend and said goodbye.
If you have the receipt, we'll exchange it right away.
Which counter do I go to for an exchange?

explain: 교환은 다른 물건으로 바꾸는 것이고 '환불'은 돈을 돌려받는 것이라서, 가게에서는 둘을 꼭 구분해서 말해요. 일상에서는 '바꾸다'도 같이 쓰지만 가게 규정에는 '교환'이 나와요. 전화번호나 선물처럼 서로 주고받을 때도 '교환하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 교환 means swapping for another item, while '환불' (refund) means getting money back, so shops keep the two clearly apart. Casual speech also uses '바꾸다', but store rules say 교환. It also works when two people give each other things, such as phone numbers or gifts.

examples.en: I took a commemorative photo with my friends at the graduation ceremony.

examples.ko: 기념사진은 가족 모두 모여서 찍기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to take the commemorative photo with the whole family together.

examples.ko: 여행지마다 기념사진이 한 장씩 남아 있어요.
examples.en: There is one commemorative photo left from each travel spot.

examples.ko: 기념사진 속 우리는 모두 활짝 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: In the commemorative photo, we are all smiling broadly.
I printed it as a commemorative photo and put it in a frame.

examples.ko: 죄송하지만 기념사진 한 장만 찍어 주시겠어요?
examples.en: Excuse me, could you take one commemorative photo for us?

explain: 졸업식, 여행, 생일처럼 기억에 남기고 싶은 날에 찍는 사진이에요. 보통 '기념사진을 찍다'라고 하고, 조금 격식 있게는 '기념 촬영'이라고도 해요. 여럿이 함께 찍으면 '단체 기념사진'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a photo taken on a day you want to remember, such as a graduation, trip or birthday. You usually say '기념사진을 찍다', and a bit more formally '기념 촬영'. A photo taken with many people is called '단체 기념사진'.

examples.en: I record the lesson every time.
I recorded it after getting the teacher's permission.
I'm going to a studio to record a song.
I recorded my voice and listened to it.
If you record the meeting, it's convenient later.

examples.ko: 지금 녹음하는 중이니까 조용히 해 주세요.
examples.en: We're recording right now, so please be quiet.

explain: '녹음하다'는 소리만 담는 일이고, 화면까지 담으면 '녹화하다'예요. 두 단어가 비슷해서 자주 헷갈려요. 녹음한 걸 '듣다', 녹화한 걸 '보다'라고 기억하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: 녹음하다 captures sound only; if the picture is included it is '녹화하다'. The two are easy to mix up. A simple trick is that you '듣다' (listen to) a 녹음 and '보다' (watch) a 녹화.

dis.h: capture sound or voice on a device

p.n: 기록하다 means you write or log the meeting, not capture the sound.

examples.en: At lunchtime I read books in the library room.
The library room is quiet, so it's good for studying.
I went to the library room and borrowed a book.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 도서실은 네 시에 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: Our school's library room closes at four o'clock.
You must not make noise in the library room.
I agreed to meet my friend in front of the library room.

explain: '도서관'이 독립된 건물이나 큰 공공 시설을 말할 때가 많다면, '도서실'은 학교나 회사 안에 있는 작은 방에 더 잘 어울려요. 그래서 학교 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '도서관' often means a standalone building or a large public facility, while '도서실' fits a small room inside a school or company. That is why it shows up often in school conversations.

examples.en: Please write your name on the back of the paper.
The phone number is on the back of the card.
I tossed a coin in the game and it came up tails.
I wrote the date on the back of the photo.

examples.ko: 숟가락 뒷면으로 달걀 껍데기를 살짝 두드려요.
examples.en: I lightly tap the eggshell with the back of a spoon.

examples.ko: 지갑 뒷면에 작은 주머니가 하나 더 있어요.
examples.en: There is one more small pocket on the back of the wallet.

explain: 납작한 물건에는 '앞면/뒷면', 방향에는 '앞쪽/뒤쪽'을 써요. 'ㅅ' 받침을 넣어 '뒷면'이라고 쓰고 [뒨면]으로 소리 나요. 동전 던지기를 할 때도 '앞면이 나왔어요'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Use '앞면/뒷면' for flat objects and '앞쪽/뒤쪽' for directions. It is spelled with the extra 'ㅅ' (뒷면) and pronounced [dwin-myeon]. In a coin toss, people say '앞면이 나왔어요' (it came up heads).

dis.h: flip side of a flat object; plain

p.n: 후면 sounds more formal and technical.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 사진기를 꼭 가져가요.
examples.en: I always take a camera when I travel.
My father's old camera still works.
We took a family photo with the new camera.

examples.ko: 사진기 배터리가 다 닳아서 사진을 못 찍었어요.
examples.en: The camera battery ran out, so I couldn't take pictures.

examples.ko: 이 사진기는 크기가 작아서 들고 다니기 편해요.
examples.en: This camera is small, so it's easy to carry around.
I borrowed my friend's camera and went to the festival.

explain: 요즘 말할 때는 '카메라'를 더 많이 써요. '사진기'는 조금 옛날 느낌이 있지만 지금도 써요. 휴대폰에 달린 카메라는 보통 '카메라'라고 해요.
explain_en: In everyday speech people now say 카메라 more often. 사진기 has a slightly old-fashioned feel but is still used. The camera on a phone is usually just called 카메라.

examples.en: The child draws a picture with colored pencils.

examples.ko: 색연필 열두 자루 한 세트를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a set of twelve colored pencils.
You sharpen colored pencils and use them like pencils.
The colored pencil broke, so I sharpened it again.
I carry colored pencils in my pencil case.
Crayons color more thickly than colored pencils.

explain: 색연필은 연필처럼 깎아서 쓰고, 크레파스는 깎지 않고 부드럽게 칠해요. 물감과 달리 물이 필요 없어요. 연필은 '자루'로 세어서 '색연필 한 자루'라고 해요.
explain_en: Colored pencils are sharpened like pencils, while crayons are not sharpened and color more softly. Unlike paint, neither needs water. Pencils are counted with 자루: '색연필 한 자루'.

examples.ko: 상처 주변을 알코올 솜으로 먼저 닦아 주세요.
examples.en: Please wipe around the wound first with an alcohol swab.

examples.ko: 이 손 소독제에는 알코올이 70퍼센트 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This hand sanitizer contains 70 percent alcohol.
Check the alcohol content on the ingredient label.

examples.ko: 병원에서 주사를 놓기 전에 알코올로 피부를 닦았어요.
examples.en: At the hospital, they wiped my skin with alcohol before the injection.

examples.ko: 알코올은 불이 잘 붙어서 조심해서 보관해야 해요.
examples.en: Alcohol catches fire easily, so you must store it carefully.

examples.ko: 알코올과 물을 섞으면 어떻게 되는지 실험했어요.
examples.en: We experimented to see what happens when you mix alcohol and water.

explain: 소독용 알코올, 성분표의 알코올 함량처럼 화학·의료 쪽에서 자주 보이는 말이에요. 마시는 것은 '술'이라고 하고, 알코올은 술이나 소독액 속에 든 성분을 가리켜요.
explain_en: This word shows up in chemistry and medicine: disinfecting alcohol, or the alcohol content on an ingredient label. A drink is called '술'; '알코올' refers to the ingredient inside drinks or disinfectant.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 주소록에 새 친구 번호를 저장했어요.
examples.en: I saved my new friend's number in my phone's address book.

examples.ko: 주소록을 정리하다가 옛 친구 이름을 찾았어요.
examples.en: While organizing my contacts, I found an old friend's name.

examples.ko: 회사 주소록에서 이름만 검색하면 번호가 나와요.
examples.en: If you search just a name in the company directory, the number appears.
The address book is so long that it's hard to find anyone.

examples.ko: 주소록에 없는 번호라서 전화를 안 받았어요.
examples.en: It was a number not in my contacts, so I didn't answer.
I sent the email address book file to my friend.

explain: 휴대폰에서는 '연락처'라고도 많이 불러요. '주소록에 저장하다', '주소록에서 찾다'처럼 쓰고, 회사에서는 직원 번호를 모아 둔 '사내 주소록'도 있어요.
explain_en: On phones it's also often called '연락처'. Say '주소록에 저장하다' (save in) or '주소록에서 찾다' (look up in). At companies there is also a '사내 주소록', a staff directory.

examples.ko: 진료실 앞에서 이름을 부를 때까지 기다려요.
examples.en: I wait in front of the exam room until they call my name.
The doctor told me to come into the exam room.
The exam room is at the right end of the second floor.
When the exam room door opened, a nurse came out.
I described my symptoms in detail in the exam room.
The child cried that he didn't want to go into the exam room.

explain: 병원에서 의사를 만나는 방은 '진료실', 입원한 사람이 지내는 방은 '병실'이에요. 주사를 맞거나 치료를 받는 방은 '처치실'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: The room where you see the doctor is a 진료실, the room where an inpatient stays is a 병실, and the room for injections or treatment is a 처치실.

examples.ko: 저는 운전할 때 팝송을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: I often listen to pop songs when I drive.

examples.ko: 영어를 배우려고 팝송 가사를 따라 불러요.
examples.en: To learn English, I sing along to pop song lyrics.

examples.ko: 이 팝송은 학교 다닐 때 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: I listened to this pop song a lot back in school.

examples.ko: 팝송 가수 중에서 좋아하는 사람이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a pop singer you like?
A pop song was playing in the cafe and it put me in a good mood.

examples.ko: 팝송으로 영어 발음을 연습하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people practice English pronunciation with pop songs.

explain: 한국어에서 '팝송'은 보통 서양, 특히 영어로 된 노래를 가리켜요. 한국 대중가요는 '가요'나 'K-팝'이라고 불러요. '팝송을 듣다', '팝송을 부르다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: In Korean, 팝송 usually means Western songs, especially ones in English. Korean pop is called 가요 or K-팝. Say '팝송을 듣다' or '팝송을 부르다'.
